Subject: SIG follow-up — Network evidence for private endpoints / allowlist

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the earlier SIG responses. Security team at Orbis has a few follow-ups specifically around network topology and allowlisting for our integration test and upcoming SOC audit window (end of Q1). Can you provide: 

- A clarified diagram that shows how Redwood Private (customer VPC) would connect to your control plane and inference endpoints (PrivateLink vs VPC Peering).
- A definitive list of IP ranges (or static egress IPs) we can add to our allowlist for callbacks, healthchecks, and webhook traffic.
- Any guidance on NAT/egress behavior for requests originating from our VPC to Redwood hosted endpoints (are there ephemeral egress IPs?).
- Recommended maintenance window for network change/testing.

We'd prefer a single consolidated packet (diagram + short answers + sample traceroute) we can upload to our compliance portal.

Appreciate fast turnaround — our auditor asked for evidence by 2026-01-20.

Regards,
Jason Liu
Director, Information Security
Orbis Technologies

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — Network evidence for private endpoints / allowlist

Hi Jason — thanks for the clear list. I'm attaching a draft "SIG network appendix" and an annotated topology diagram. Quick summary below; detailed answers are in the PDF.

Short answers:
- Private connectivity options: we support both AWS PrivateLink (recommended for cross-account private endpoints with fine-grained access) and VPC Peering (possible but we generally avoid peering across customer-owned VPCs due to routing complexity).
- Static egress IPs: For hosted customers we can provide a small set of stable egress IPs via our Egress Gateway (see attached CSV). For Dedicated/Private deployments customers retain full control of egress.
- Ephemeral egress: When traffic flows through our multi-tenant hosted nodes without Egress Gateway config, egress IPs can be ephemeral; we call these out explicitly in the appendix.
- Maintenance/testing: suggest a 2-hour window (low-traffic 02:00-04:00 UTC) for traceroutes and connectivity tests; we'll coordinate with your network team.

Vivek: can you confirm the exact CSV contents and add any traceroute samples we can ship? Karthik: please review the diagram text and confirm wording about PrivateLink endpoints.

Thanks — attaching: redwood_sig-network-appendix-draft.pdf, redwood_vpc-architecture-annotated.png

Best,

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — Network evidence for private endpoints / allowlist

Naomi / Karthik — added technical details below for the packet to Jason. Please paste these into the appendix and attach redwood_static-egress-ip-list.csv.

Technical details (for appendix):
- PrivateLink: We expose an endpoint service in the region; customers create interface endpoints in their VPC. Traffic stays within the AWS network, security groups control access. Recommended when customers do NOT want route propagation or transitive routing.

- VPC Peering: Supported but only for single-account peering. Peering requires explicit route table updates and can complicate cross-account pathing. Not recommended for customers wanting simple private connectivity to our control plane across org boundaries.

- Egress IPs & NAT: For hosted API calls originating at Redwood to customer callbacks (webhooks) we can route outbound traffic through a managed Egress Gateway that advertises a small set of static IPv4 addresses. Attached CSV contains the current advertised set (CIDR /32 list for each failling endpoint). Note these are subject to quarterly rotation with advance notice; we include rotation windows and replacement ranges in SLA attachments.

- Traceroute/sample: Example traceroute to a PrivateLink interface endpoint will show AWS internal hops only; for peering you'll see direct peering hop entries. If you need, we can run a traceroute from an active node to one of your test endpoints during the scheduled window and provide raw output.

- TLS and auth: All control-plane communications are mutual TLS-authenticated and our service certificate chain is included in the appendix. No client-side certs required for PrivateLink.

Operational ask: please confirm which option you prefer (PrivateLink vs peering) and provide a care-of contact + IP allowlist CIDR(s) we should expect for inbound healthchecks. We'll then set up a short connectivity test (15–30 mins) and provide logs.

Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
